svg.title: ViT: patches become tokens; CLIP aligns image–text
svg.desc: ViT divides an image into non-overlapping patches, projects them to token embeddings, adds a CLS token and positions, then uses a standard Transformer encoder. CLIP uses separate image and text encoders with contrastive training so matched pairs score higher than mismatched pairs, enabling zero-shot prompt matching.

g.text: ViT: patches become tokens; CLIP aligns image–text
ViT uses a standard encoder; CLIP learns a shared image–text space.
Zero-shot: choose the class prompt closest to the image.
